title: Controlling quantum state transfer in rooted products
summary: Godsil and McKay (1978) showed that the rooted product is a powerful tool for constructing non-isomorphic cospectral pairs of graphs. Despite lacking a convenient tensor product structure, we show that the rooted product is useful for constructing graphs with good quantum state transfer properties. In particular, we prove a simple transference principle: if a graph $X$ has quantum state transfer and $Y$ is a controllable graph, their rooted product $X^Y$ has quantum state transfer (inherited from $X$).
